Glue — grammar

ràng/jiào causative

Template: ràng/jiào + person + action (+result)

"make/let someone do" — requests, permissions, orders

Ràng tā shìshi ba.
Māma jiào wǒ qù mǎi cài.

Foreigner traps

  • shǐ is the written causative — understand it in print, say ràng/jiào.
  • ràng also marks the passive: wǒ ràng tā qì sǐ le (he drove me crazy) — ràng + person + verb is 'make them do'; subject + ràng + person is 'it was done to me'.
  • jiào doubles as the hail: jiào fúwùyuán — calling and causing share one syllable; context splits them.

a and its variants

Template: sentence-final a; after vowels ya, after -n na, after -u/-o wa, la = le + a fused

warmth, urgency, seeking agreement

Kuài yìdiǎn ya, yào chídào le.
Nǐ zěnme cái lái wa.

Foreigner traps

  • One family: ya/na/wa are all a after vowels / -n / -u/-o — don't memorize four particles.
  • la already contains le: zhīdào la = got it ALREADY — stacking la + le doubles the past.
  • ba proposes, a warms: zǒu ba (let's go) pushes; zǒu a (we're going, right?) agrees — pick your push.

Recall quiz

Native notes — ràng's two jobs, pressing politely, and hotpot protocol

ràng lets — and lets you be done in

Causative ràng wǒ lái (let me) covers offers, permissions, orders. But ràng and jiào also mark the passive: wǒ ràng tā qì sǐ le — he drove me crazy. Same syllable, opposite victim. Word order is the tell: ràng + person + verb is 'make someone do'; subject + ràng + person is 'someone did it to me'.

dàodǐ turns up the heat

Nǐ dàodǐ qù bù qù? presses after dodges — fine between close friends, aggressive from acquaintances or at work. Soften with jiūjìng or keep dàodǐ about the matter, not the person: zhège dàodǐ shì zěnme huí shì. If someone aims it at you, they've run out of patience — answer, don't dodge again.

Hotpot is a social institution, not a meal

In Chongqing huǒguō is the default gathering: one pot, collective ordering, everyone's chopsticks in. You'll be asked là bù là — wēilà (mildly spicy) is the local compromise and saying it wins respect. Rice refills (jiā yì wǎn mǐfàn) are flagged to the fúwùyuán by voice, hands busy. Plan nothing after; nobody leaves on time.

ya / na / wa / la are one particle

They're all sentence-final a wearing sound-change coats: after vowels ya, after -n na, after -u/-o wa, and la is le + a fused into one syllable. Texting writes exactly what the mouth does — hǎo ya, duì a, zǒu la. Treat them as one warm coating, not four vocabulary items, and your typing starts sounding spoken.
